name: Pye Records
ownershipStory: Founded in 1953 when the Pye electronics company, better known for making radios and televisions, bought the independent label Nixa and turned it into Pye Nixa. It signed the Kinks in the mid-1960s on a standard-for-the-era contract that gave the band little long-term control over their masters. In 1980 the rights to the Pye name ran out and the label carried on as PRT (Precision Records and Tapes), which is why the map ends Pye there. The Pye name was bought and relaunched as a small label in 2024.
hook: A television and radio manufacturer that happened to also make some of the biggest British Invasion records.
blurb: Pye began in 1953 as the record label of an electronics manufacturer. By the mid-1960s it was releasing hits by bands like the Kinks, usually on contracts that gave the band little control over their own recordings. It is a reminder that Britain's 1960s guitar-band boom was still built on the same standard contracts, bad for artists, as the rest of the pop business of the time.
